title: Man in the Car Paradox
supportedClaims: People buy status objects hoping to be admired, but observers usually admire themselves in the object rather than the owner behind it.
The human mind projects desire onto visible symbols while paying far less attention to the person using them than that person imagines.
The practical move is to aim money at values that genuinely matter to you rather than purchases designed to borrow social meaning from the outside.
caution: Status signals can still influence other people, but they are a thin and unstable route to dignity.
